headline: US blue-wave fears over AI-data-centre rules crash KOSPI 5.3% on record foreign selling: KTBs rally hard, 10Y −8.1bp to 3.887% (lowest since April) and 3s10s flattens to 21.8bp, stopping our steepener
summary: KTBs rallied for a third day, led by 5–10Y: the 10Y fell 8.1bp to 3.887% and the 5Y 6.8bp to 3.769%, against −4.5bp for the 3Y (3.669%, lowest since Aug 5) and −1.1bp for the 1Y (3.567%). The long end lagged, with 20Y −6.2bp and 30Y/50Y −5.5bp to 3.998%/4.021%, so 3s10s flattened 3.6bp to 21.8bp (flattest since April 2025) while 10s30s steepened 2.6bp to 11.1bp. The front end stayed pinned by November hike pricing: MSB 91-day 3.179% and CD 3.34% were unchanged and CP held at 3.83%, keeping CP–CD at 49bp (97th percentile). Spread products did not follow the rally: AA- 3Y fell 4.2bp to 69bp over KTB, KEPCO 3Y is a 1-year wide 44bp over, AAA bank 1Y 44bp over (98th percentile) and the KDB 1Y fit widened 5bp to 35bp, though KDB 3Y tightened 3bp to 25bp.
drivers: Fears that a Democratic Congress will tighten rules on AI data centres hit chips: KOSPI fell 300 points (−5.28%) to 5,383.80, Samsung −7.6% and SK Hynix −9.5%, and a sell-side sidecar was triggered. Foreigners sold a record KRW 3.39tn of KOSPI stock, a fifth straight day, while individuals (2.27tn) and institutions (0.85tn) bought. The bond rally gathered pace as stocks fell, which makes this the main driver of the day.
US Treasuries explain only a quarter of it

On the New York close the US 10Y par yield fell about 5bp to 4.90% on the election, an unchanged refunding ($58bn 3Y, $42bn 10Y, $25bn 30Y next week), a softer ISM services index (54.5 vs 54.8 expected, prices paid 73.0) and an 8% drop in oil. At the 1-year daily beta of 0.46 that implies −2.3bp for the KTB 10Y; the actual −8.1bp leaves about −5.8bp local, and since Seoul had already priced much of the Treasury rally on Wednesday, today's move was almost all Korea. The KTB–UST 10Y gap widened to −101bp, another 1-year extreme.

Foreigners sold 555 3Y KTB futures but bought 663 10Y, and the 10Y contract rose 69 ticks to 109.19, the 30Y 132 ticks to 117.20 and the 3Y 14 ticks to 103.69. Against our basket fair values (3Y 103.82, 10Y 109.23, 30Y 117.11) the 3Y settled 13 ticks cheap (about 4.5bp), the 10Y 4 ticks cheap and the 30Y 9 ticks rich: the market bid for long duration, not the front end.
Front end anchored by the BOK

The 3Y now sits only 67bp over the 3.00% base rate, the narrowest in nine months; with a 3.50% terminal rate the common view and a November 26 hike priced, dealers see 3.6% on the 3Y as a floor, which pushed buying into the 5–10Y. A record September current-account surplus (USD 61.5bn) supports the won but did not move bonds; USD/KRW ended at 1,342.1, up 0.6 won despite the equity outflow.
data: Record, first month above USD 60bn; supports the won and the BOK's hawkish lean, little KTB impact.
In line to a touch soft; the fuel price cap flatters headline, so it does not rule out a November 26 hike.
Strong end-user demand; the 30Y now trades about 7bp below the auction yield.
Trade strength underpins the won and the BOK's hawkish lean.
Fastest output gain since 2011; keeps hike pricing in the 1–2Y.
Large beat on chip capex and government spending; private consumption fell 0.2%.
Hold at 3.00%, unanimous (after +25bp in July and August)
Guided to staying restrictive; a November 26 hike to 3.25% remains the front-end base case.
view: This is now a local equity-to-bond rotation, not a Treasury trade: over four weeks the 10Y is −51bp, of which about −23bp is US Treasuries at a weekly beta of 0.62 and −27bp is Korea's own, and today only about 2bp of the 8bp rally came from New York. The rotation signal rose to +1.93 (bond rally, from +1.76 a week ago) as foreigners sold a record KRW 3.4tn and margin credit kept falling, and the curve has priced it hard: the 3Y sits 17bp above a 3.50% terminal while the 10Y has fallen twice as much. With a November 26 hike still priced, a 3Y floor near 3.60% and US payrolls and 3Y/10Y/30Y auctions next week, I expect the 10Y to hold 3.80–3.98% over the next two weeks; I would not chase below 3.85% and would buy a back-up toward 4.00%. Our 3s10s steepener was stopped at today's close (21.8bp vs 25bp stop, a 7.2bp loss from 29bp); I stay flat on the curve until KOSPI stabilises, because the flattening is a direct readout of equity outflows. The signal still works best against Treasuries: hedged with about 0.6 × US 10Y, rally calls hit 66% and sell-off calls 69% (48% and 57% outright), Sharpe 1.31 against 0.99, so a beta-hedged KTB long remains the cleaner expression than adding outright duration at the widest KTB–UST gap of the year.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y fell 3.2bp to 3.655% (66th percentile of its 1-year range, average 3.36%) and the 1Y only 1.1bp to 3.567% (86th), so the front end again lagged. MSB 91-day is 3.179% (97th percentile) and 1s2s is 8.8bp (1st percentile, average 30bp): the market still prices a November 26 hike, and the 3Y is only 67bp over the base rate.
buckets.call: No trigger hit. Add 2Y above 3.80%; fade rallies below 3.60%.

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s flattened 3.6bp to 21.8bp, the flattest since April 2025 and the bottom of its 1-year range (average 40bp), as the 10Y rallied 8.1bp against 4.5bp for a 3Y held up by hike pricing. Our steepener from 29bp closed through its 25bp stop: stopped, −7.2bp. Foreigners bought 10Y and sold 3Y futures, so the flattening is flow-driven and can run while stocks fall.
buckets.call: Closed at 21.8bp (stopped). Re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures) only once KOSPI holds a rebound for a week; then target 30bp, stop 18bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.887% is at the 48th percentile of a 3.13–4.60% range (average 3.90%), 12bp lower this week and 51bp lower over four weeks. The KTB–UST gap of −101bp is the widest of the year and the old 4.10–4.15% buy zone looks out of reach for now.
buckets.call: Buy zone moved to 3.98–4.02% (was 4.10–4.15%, never reached); stop 4.12%, target 3.82%. Don't chase below 3.85%.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s is unchanged at +2.3bp, the 93rd percentile (average −9.6bp); both fell 5.5bp, so the switch from +2.5bp is still 0.2bp in our favour. The long end lagged the 10Y (10s30s +2.6bp to 11.1bp). On Wednesday's trades the 2054 KTB (24-8) was about 7bp cheap to the curve but on only 6 trades; the 3Y-futures bonds 25-10 and 25-4 were 3–4bp rich.
buckets.call: Keep the 30Y into 50Y switch at +2.5bp; target −3bp, stop +6bp. Open, 0.2bp in favour.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: The KDB fit (20 trades) puts the 3Y 24.8bp over KTB, down 3.1bp and at the 80th percentile (average 19bp); that is 1.2bp in our favour. The 1Y widened 5bp to 35bp (95th) and KOFIA's 1Y KDB quote is 33bp over (92nd, average 23bp). KEXIM shows 20bp, but on 4 trades, so low confidence.
buckets.call: Hold the overweight from ~26bp; take profit at 20bp, cut above 35bp. Open, 1.2bp in favour.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (47-trade fit) is 44bp over the 1Y KTB, the 98th percentile (average 31bp), and 37bp at 2Y (89th). CD (3.34%) and CP (3.83%) were unchanged, so CP–CD stays 49bp (97th percentile, average 28bp). IBK 1Y at 38bp over (12 trades) is at its 1-year wide.
buckets.call: No change: prefer KDB over bank debentures; revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y fell 4.2bp to 4.358%, about in step with the KTB, leaving the spread at 69bp (82nd percentile, average 61bp); KEPCO 3Y at 44bp over is a new 1-year wide. Spreads held through a 5% equity crash, but there is no turn in stocks to buy into.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI holds a rebound for a week; no trigger hit.

ktb:3.note: Lowest since Aug 5; 67bp over base rate

ktb:10.note: Lowest since April; UST explains ~2bp of 8

watch: Next: US October payrolls (Fri Nov 6), US 3Y/10Y/30Y auctions (Nov 9, 10, 12), Korea November 1–10 exports around Nov 11, then the BOK meeting on Nov 26; a KOSPI rebound with foreigners turning buyers, or a Treasury sell-off on payrolls or weak auctions, is the main risk to the rally.
sources: Etoday (bond close, futures flows and settles)
